why: No physical arm64 phone was reachable from this environment (cloud container, no USB, no device farm). The brief requires a REAL arm64 phone for this verdict; nothing below substitutes for it.

required.what: the APK's OCR self-test on a physical arm64-v8a phone, run once from the app
required.where: Dodaj dom z linku → section "Test zgodności odczytu wymiarów" → "Uruchom test"

pass.exact: 92 of 96 ("zgodne z korpusem testowym (to nie miara dokładności)")

required.fail: NIEZGODNY z komputerem, a different corpus hash ("Telefon narysował inne etykiety…"), or any "Test nie powiódł się"

supplementary.kind: arm64 Linux user-mode emulation on an x86-64 desktop (QEMU qemu-aarch64-static) — NOT a phone, NOT Android, NOT arm64 silicon
supplementary.bundle: the runtime bundle built locally at 5315ff8 (PRE_HOLDOUT_7_SHA) with apps/local-analyzer/build.mjs: main.mjs sha256 f1a69daac12fba70…, ocr-self-test.mjs, ocr-worker.mjs, the WebAssembly and the model, run as `node main.mjs --self-test ocr --watchdog-scale 20`. Against the OWNER APK (run 160): main.mjs, the WASM, its loader and the model are byte-identical; analyzer.mjs, ocr-worker.mjs and ocr-self-test.mjs are identical apart from esbuild's source-path comments and module keys (the APK build runs from apps/android/app)

attempts.outcome: SELF_TEST_FAILED after 909 s — "the recogniser worker gave no sign of life for 120 s while reading a label"
attempts.cause: an emulated CPU compiles and runs the WebAssembly ~75× slower than native; the production watchdog (120 s per label) is correct for a phone and wrong for QEMU. `--watchdog-scale` (self-test only, 1–100, the app never passes it) was added before the freeze for this measurement.

attempts.timingNote: emulated: not a phone's timing and not a basis for any performance claim

supplementary.whatItShows: The arm64 build of Node 18 with the same bundle, WebAssembly and model draws the same corpus and reads it to the same bytes as the x86-64 desktop, Node 22, Node 18 without ICU and the x86_64 Android emulator. It exercises the arm64 code paths of V8's WebAssembly compiler under emulation; it does not exercise nodejs-mobile, Android's process limits, a phone's memory pressure or arm64 silicon.
